'''Javier García Portillo''' (born 30 March 1982) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[forward (association football)|forward]].

He started out at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and appeared in 59 competitive games during his tenure, scoring 17 goals. In [[La Liga]], he also played for [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona|Gimnàstic]], [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] and [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] for a total of 131 matches and 21 goals, and also competed professionally in Italy and Belgium.<ref name=LP>[https://www.laprovincia.es/ud-las-palmas/2015/12/29/portillo-ex-ud-35-partidos-9986301.html Portillo, ex de la UD con 35 partidos, se retira en el Hércules (Portillo, former UD man with 35 matches, retires at Hércules)]; [[La Provincia (Canary Islands)|La Provincia]], 29 December 2015 (in Spanish)</ref>

In a 14-year senior career, Portillo represented Hércules in all three major [[Spanish football league system|levels of Spanish football]].

==Club career==
Portillo was born in [[Aranjuez]], [[Community of Madrid]]. In 1994, aged 12, he entered [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth system. Over seven seasons he was a prolific scorer, netting 370 goals and breaking a record previously held by [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]].<ref>[https://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/abci-portillo-bestia-blanca-200111100300-59406_noticia.html Portillo, la bestia blanca del gol (Portillo, the goal's white beast)]; [[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]], 10 November 2001 (in Spanish)</ref> In August 2002, he signed his first professional contract, running until 2006 with a [[buyout clause]] of [[Euro|€]]15 million.<ref>[https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2002/08/28/madrid-mantiene-clausula-portillo/0003_1208558.htm El Madrid mantiene la cláusula a Portillo (Madrid keep Portillo's clause)]; [[La Voz de Galicia]], 28 August 2002 (in Spanish)</ref>

On 6 October 2002, Portillo made his first [[La Liga]] appearance and second overall for the main squad, starting in a 5–2 home win over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]]<ref>[https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2002/10/06/liga/1033930280.html Ronaldo irrumpe con dos goles en media hora (Ronaldo bursts with two goals in thirty minutes)]; [[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]], 6 October 2002 (in Spanish)</ref> and ending [[2002–03 La Liga|that season]] with five goals in only ten games. He also scored a vital [[Last-minute goal|last-minute]] equaliser against [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]] second group phase, a goal which ultimately proved to be crucial to reach [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|the knockout stages]].<ref>[https://www.rsssf.org/players/portillo-in-ec.html Javier García Portillo – Matches in European Cups]; at [[RSSSF]]</ref>

Portillo was loaned to [[Serie A]] side [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in July 2004, but was recalled by new manager [[Vanderlei Luxemburgo]], who arrived midway through the [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05 campaign]].<ref>[https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/01/13/futbol/1105633609.html Portillo regresa al Real Madrid (Portillo returns to Real Madrid)]; El Mundo, 14 January 2005 (in Spanish)</ref> However, the same coach deemed him surplus to requirements and another loan ensued, to [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] of the [[Belgian Pro League]].<ref>[https://es.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01ac-0e6cdc3fedc4-fc7a82033c97-1000--portillo-cedido-al-brujas/ Portillo, cedido al Brujas (Portillo, loaned to Brugge)]; UEFA, 31 August 2005 (in Spanish)</ref>

At the end of this loan period, Portillo returned to Real under newly hired coach [[Fabio Capello]]. With new signing [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] adding to already present Raúl, [[Antonio Cassano]] and [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], he was released and signed a two-year contract with recently promoted [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]].<ref>[https://elpais.com/deportes/2006/08/07/actualidad/1154935319_850215.html El Real Madrid traspasa a Portillo al Nástic de Tarragona (Real Madrid transfer Portillo to Nástic de Tarragona)]; [[El País]], 7 August 2006 (in Spanish)</ref>

After a successful individual season (12 goals in all competitions, although the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] were [[2006–07 La Liga|relegated]] from the top flight),<ref>[https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2017/10/30/nastic/843084-que-fue-de-javier-portillo.html ¿Qué fue de Javier Portillo? (What happened to Javier Portillo?)]; Vavel, 30 October 2017 (in Spanish)</ref> in July 2007 Portillo replaced at Osasuna [[Roberto Soldado]], who returned from loan to Real Madrid.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121023222754/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=553034.html Duo boost Osasuna forward line]; UEFA, 19 June 2007</ref> He was used irregularly in his first two years, and only netted three times in the league.

In late December 2009, Portillo – who was only fourth or fifth-choice striker for Osasuna coach [[José Antonio Camacho]]<ref>[https://www.marca.com/2009/09/01/futbol/equipos/osasuna/1251807556.html Osasuna no coloca a Portillo y Nico Medina se queda sin ficha (Osasuna cannot relocate Portillo and Nico Medina is not registered)]; [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]], 1 September 2009 (in Spanish)</ref>– finally moved clubs, signing until the end of [[2009–10 Segunda División|the season]] plus two more with [[Segunda División]]'s [[Hércules CF|Hércules]]. After some time to adjust he finished in the starting XI, netting vital goals in the final stretch, including one in the last round for a 2–0 victory at [[Real Unión]] as the [[Alicante]] side returned to the first division after 13 years.<ref>[https://www.marca.com/2010/06/19/futbol/2adivision/1276970500.html El Hércules vuelve a Primera y condena al Real Unión (Hércules return to ''Primera'' and condemn Real Unión)]; Marca, 19 June 2010 (in Spanish)</ref>

Portillo returned to reserve status in [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11]], after Hércules signed [[David Trezeguet]] and [[Nelson Valdez]] in the off-season.<ref>[https://www.diarioinformacion.com/hercules-cf/2010/11/30/valdez-trezeguet-sociedad-gol/1070082.html Valdez-Trezeguet, la sociedad del gol (Valdez-Trezeguet, the goal society)]; Diario Información, 30 November 2010 (in Spanish)</ref> He only started through injury or suspension to the pair, and scored just twice in official matches, one coming in a 3–1 away defeat of [[Real Sociedad]] on 3 April 2011,<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301825?cc=5739 Hercules claim giant win] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024164335/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301825?cc=5739|date=24 October 2012}}; [[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]], 3 April 2011</ref> with Hércules being immediately relegated.

On 2 August 2011, Portillo signed for three years with [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] in the second tier.<ref>[http://www.udlaspalmas.es/actualidad-noticias-1858 La UD Las Palmas ficha al delantero Portillo por tres temporadas (UD Las Palmas sign forward Portillo for three seasons] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110918164555/http://www.udlaspalmas.es/actualidad-noticias-1858|date=18 September 2011}}; UD Las Palmas, 2 August 2011 (in Spanish)</ref> For the [[2012–13 Segunda División|2012–13 season]], however, he moved teams again, returning to Hércules on a three-year deal.<ref>[http://www.herculesdealicantecf.es/noticias/portillo-regresa-al-hercules Portillo regresa al Hércules (Portillo returns to Hércules)] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130217114215/http://www.herculesdealicantecf.es/noticias/portillo-regresa-al-hercules|date=17 February 2013}}; Hércules CF, 2 August 2012 (in Spanish)</ref>

In late December 2015, Portillo announced his retirement at the age of 33.<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/2015/12/28/mas_futbol/1451302677_335432.html Portillo se retira a los 33 años: "Es el momento idóneo" (Portillo retires at the age of 33: "This is the right moment")]; [[Diario AS]], 28 December 2015 (in Spanish)</ref> Subsequently, he worked as his last club's [[director of football]].<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/2019/09/04/mas_futbol/1567577607_855359.html Portillo: "Esta es de las mejores plantillas que hemos tenido" (Portillo: "This is one of the best squads we have ever had")]; Diario AS, 4 September 2019 (in Spanish)</ref>

==International career==
Making his debut in 2002 – shortly after his arrival at the Real Madrid senior setup – Portillo played ten times for [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21s]], and scored five goals.<ref>[https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2002/10/15/futbol/1034713412.html Los Sub'21 tumban a Eslovenia con tres golpes (The Under'21s down Slovenia with three blows)]; El Mundo, 15 October 2002 (in Spanish)</ref><ref>[https://hemeroteca.abc.es/nav/Navigate.exe/hemeroteca/madrid/abc/2002/11/20/095.html Portillo abrió el camino al festival goleador sub 21 (Portillo paved way for under 21 scoring festival)]; [[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]], 20 November 2002 (in Spanish)</ref><ref>[https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2003/04/01/futbol_internacional/1049231322.html Los sub'21 se conforman con endosar una 'manita' a Armenia (Under'21s settle with handing Armenia a 'fiver')]; El Mundo, 2 April 2003 (in Spanish)</ref>
